definition: Exalt means to glorify — to lift someone or something high in praise, above everything around it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word exalt. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know exalt should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Sports radio spent the whole week exalting the rookie goalie, replaying her double save until the clip wore thin.
Praise is the ground floor — sincere approval, no pedestal yet; exalting begins where plain praise leaves off.
Deify goes further than exalt — to exalt heroes is to raise them high; to deify them is to stop calling them human at all.

To glorify is to bathe a person or deed in glory — praise polished until it shines. To exalt is to lift the subject bodily above everything around it, onto the pedestal. Both stay on the human side of the line: a glorified general and an exalted one are still men, just brightly lit.

To idolize is to worship someone the way a fan worships a star — adoration that lives in the admirer's own heart. To exalt is a public act: hymns, monuments, speeches that lift the subject high for all to see. Idolizing happens inside you; exalting is performed out loud.
